title: A failed run, one snapshot-marked holding, and no recorded trade decisions
body_html:
A failed run, one snapshot-marked holding, and no recorded trade decisions

Paper trading · 2026-11-02T17:00:14.700715-05:00

The supplied context ends at 5:00:14 p.m. ET on Nov. 2 and uses recorded snapshots, not a guaranteed closing-price feed. The daily run scheduled for 3:15 p.m. failed about a minute later because the research planner context exceeded its configured limit. There is no completed book evaluation in the supplied records, and no order, deterministic risk, or fill records to establish a proposal, approval or rejection, or execution. The paper account snapshot shows $2,000 cash and equity. The mean-reversion book has a recorded MU holding marked from a 4:56:11 p.m. observation; its marked equity is about $2.67 above starting cash, but that snapshot-based amount is unrealized and excludes fees.

Today's lesson: A marked gain is not a realized gain

A snapshot-based gain is an estimate, not a sale result. For MU, $990.00 observed midpoint minus $939.88 average purchase price is $50.12 per share; multiplied by 0.053191 shares, that is about $2.67 unrealized gain before fees. The observation was recorded at 4:56:11 p.m. ET, and the bid-ask spread was wide, so the estimate has uncertainty.

Every holding

MU — mean-reversion

The mean-reversion book records 0.053191 MU shares at an average purchase price of $939.88 per share, excluding fees. Its observed midpoint was $990.00 at 4:56:11 p.m. ET on Nov. 2, giving a recorded market value of $52.6591 and unrealized gain of $2.6659, excluding fees. The midpoint comes from a recorded bid of $841.87 and ask of $1,138.13; this is a snapshot, not a live or guaranteed closing price. The supplied records contain no current investment reasoning for MU and no fill event showing when or how this holding was established. The wide bid-ask range and snapshot-based valuation are the strongest recorded reasons to treat the gain as uncertain.

Read the timestamps with the numbers

The account snapshot is from 5:00:14 p.m. ET; the MU price observation is earlier, at 4:56:11 p.m. ET. The quote's $990 midpoint is calculated from a recorded $841.87 bid and $1,138.13 ask. Because snapshots may precede fills, timing matters when comparing a mark with any trade record.

What to watch next

Check whether the scheduled run completes, then read the records separately: what was proposed, what deterministic risk approved or rejected, and whether a broker fill or simulated fill actually occurred. Compare snapshot times with any fills, since an older snapshot may come first.

Unrealized gain: A recorded estimate of a holding's value before it is sold. Here it uses the observed bid-ask midpoint and excludes fees.

Bid-ask midpoint: The midpoint between the recorded bid and ask. It is an observation at a specific time, not necessarily a price at which a trade could be made.

Data timing and limitations

Prices come from recorded snapshots, not a guaranteed closing-price feed.
Paper account holdings use the latest recorded snapshot, which may precede fills.
Book marks use observed bid/ask midpoints at price_as_of, not guaranteed live prices. Without an admitted quote the value remains unknown; book gains exclude fees.
Work starting after the cutoff is outside this report. Failures remain labelled.
